```text
---
scope: templates, modules/templates
verified-at: c0092050a4
---

# templates — the Go HTML templates and their helpers

**Read when:** editing a page's markup, adding a template, or needing a template function.
**Not here:** the handler that renders it -> `routers-web.md`; classes -> `frontend-css.md`; behaviour -> `frontend-js.md`.

## Responsibilities

Server-rendered HTML, composed with Go's `html/template`. `modules/templates` owns the renderer and
every function templates can call.

| Directory | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `base/` | the page skeleton: `head.tmpl`, `head_script.tmpl`, `head_navbar.tmpl`, `footer.tmpl`, `paginate.tmpl`, `alert.tmpl` |
| `shared/` | reusable partials: `issuelist.tmpl`, `combomarkdowneditor.tmpl`, `actions/`, `secrets/`, `webhook/`, `user/` |
| `repo/`, `user/`, `org/`, `admin/`, `explore/`, `projects/`, `package/` | one directory per page area |
| `mail/` | email bodies |
| `status/` | error pages |
| `devtest/` | the `/devtest` component gallery, also driven by the e2e tests |
| `custom/` | site-admin override hooks — intentionally near-empty |
| `swagger/` | the generated API spec (`v1_json.tmpl`), see `routers-api-v1.md` |

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `modules/templates/helper.go` | `newFuncMapWebPage` — the whole set of page template functions, including `dict`, `Iif` and `Eval` |
| `modules/templates/util_render.go`, `util_render_comment.go` | markup and comment rendering helpers |
| `modules/templates/util_date.go`, `util_avatar.go`, `util_string.go`, `util_slice.go`, `util_dict.go` | the rest of the function set, grouped by kind |
| `modules/templates/htmlrenderer.go` | `TplName` and the renderer |
| `modules/templates/scopedtmpl/` | the scoped-template machinery behind partial rendering |
| `templates/base/head_script.tmpl` | emits `window.config`, including `pageData` |

## Conventions & invariants

- A template is addressed by its path under `templates/` without the extension, as a
  `templates.TplName` constant in the handler — `"repo/issue/list"` is
  `templates/repo/issue/list.tmpl` (`routers-web.md`).
- **The handler's `ctx.Data` is the only data channel.** A template cannot reach anything the
  handler did not put there, and `ctx.RootData` inside a template context is that same data.
- Data destined for JavaScript goes through `ctx.PageData`, which `base/head_script.tmpl` emits as
  `window.config.pageData` — a separate channel from `ctx.Data`.
- **Every user-visible string is a locale key**, written `{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.issues.new"}}` or
  `ctx.Locale.TrN` for plurals. Never a literal. Keys are added only to
  `options/locale/locale_en-US.json`; the other locales come from Crowdin.
- Composition is `{{template "base/head" .}}` style includes. New shared markup goes in `shared/`,
  not copied between areas.
- `dict` is lowercase for historical reasons; new template functions get uppercase names
  (`helper.go` says so at the definition).
- Mail templates use a different, smaller function set — `mailBodyFuncMap` and
  `mailSubjectTextFuncMap` in `modules/templates/mail.go`. A helper added for pages is not
  available in `templates/mail/`.
- Class attributes are written as one readable unit including their conditionals
  (`frontend-css.md`).
- Hook frontend behaviour up declaratively with `data-global-init` / `data-global-click`
  attributes rather than inline script (`frontend-js.md`).
- `.tmpl` files are tab-indented (`.editorconfig`).

## Recipes

**Add a page's template.** Create the `.tmpl` under the matching area directory, include
`base/head` and `base/footer`, declare the `TplName` constant in the handler, and add every string
as a locale key.

**Share markup between pages.** Put the partial in `templates/shared/` and include it from both
places. Two near-identical partials in two area directories is the thing to avoid.

**Add a template function.** Add it to the map returned by `newFuncMapWebPage` in
`modules/templates/helper.go` and implement it in the matching `util_*.go`. Prefer passing prepared data from the handler — a function that
does database work at render time is a performance bug.

**See a component in isolation.** Run Gitea in development mode and open `/devtest`.

## Gotchas

- A misspelled key in `ctx.Data` renders as empty, not as an error. Check the handler when
  something is silently blank.
- A missing locale key renders the key itself — visible, but easy to miss in a rarely-hit branch.
- `templates/swagger/v1_json.tmpl` is generated. Edit the swagger comments and run
  `make generate-swagger` instead (`routers-api-v1.md`).
- `templates/custom/` is for deployment overrides, not a place to put course code.

## Related

- `routers-web.md` — `TplName` and `ctx.Data`
- `frontend-css.md`, `frontend-js.md` — the classes and attributes used here
```

156	// Releases render releases list page
157	func Releases(ctx *context.Context) {
158		ctx.Data["PageIsReleaseList"] = true
159		ctx.Data["Title"] = ctx.Tr("repo.release.releases")
160	
161		listOptions := db.ListOptions{
162			Page:     ctx.FormInt("page"),
163			PageSize: ctx.FormInt("limit"),
164		}
165		if listOptions.PageSize == 0 {
166			listOptions.PageSize = setting.Repository.Release.DefaultPagingNum
167		}
168		if listOptions.PageSize > setting.API.MaxResponseItems {
169			listOptions.PageSize = setting.API.MaxResponseItems
170		}
171	
172		writeAccess := ctx.Repo.Permission.CanWrite(unit.TypeReleases)
173		ctx.Data["CanCreateRelease"] = writeAccess && !ctx.Repo.Repository.IsArchived
174	
175		releases, err := getReleaseInfos(ctx, &repo_model.FindReleasesOptions{
176			ListOptions: listOptions,
177			// only show draft releases for users who can write, read-only users shouldn't see draft releases.
178			IncludeDrafts: writeAccess,
179			RepoID:        ctx.Repo.Repository.ID,
180		})
181		if err != nil {
182			ctx.ServerError("getReleaseInfos", err)
183			return
184		}
185		for _, rel := range releases {
186			if rel.Release.IsTag && rel.Release.Title == "" {
187				rel.Release.Title = rel.Release.TagName
188			}
189		}
190	
191		ctx.Data["Releases"] = releases
192	
193		numReleases := ctx.Data["NumReleases"].(int64)
194		pager := context.NewPagination(numReleases, listOptions.PageSize, listOptions.Page, 5)
195		pager.AddParamFromRequest(ctx.Req)
196		ctx.Data["Page"] = pager
197		ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplReleasesList)
198	}

# Issue #1 — Show a message when a repository has no releases

## Context
Issue #1 (opened by musta55, assigned to Carson): `/{owner}/{repo}/releases` on a repo with no
releases renders the header and an empty `<ul id="release-list">` — a blank page. Goal: show a
friendly empty state, and for users who can create releases, a call to action.

Housekeeping already done: switched to `main` (up to date with origin). Nothing was deleted: the
previous checkout was a *detached HEAD* at `origin/chore/claude-students-docs`, which has no local
branch and is the head of **open PR #8** — deleting the remote branch would close that PR. Untracked
`ai-logs/sprint0/CarsonRackley/` was kept.

PR #8 takeaway: it adds `.claude-students/` (INDEX + `docs/` + plain-English `guide/` twins),
`STUDENTS.md`, and `.specstory` in `.gitignore`. It is not on `main` yet, so its docs are read via
`git show origin/chore/claude-students-docs:.claude-students/docs/<name>.md`. Relevant ones here:
`templates.md`, `routers-web.md`, `i18n.md`, `testing.md`.

Course-process note: D5 requires concept location *without AI first*. Before implementing, trace
the route yourself (`routers/web/web.go` → `repo.Releases` in `routers/web/repo/release.go:157`
→ `templates/repo/release/list.tmpl`) so the AI log shows AI confirming, not replacing, that step.

## Approach — template-only empty state, reusing the existing `empty-placeholder` pattern
No Go/handler change: `Releases()` already puts `Releases`, `CanCreateRelease`, and `RepoLink`
into `ctx.Data`. Existing precedent to copy: `templates/projects/list.tmpl:79-84`
(`<div class="empty-placeholder">` + 48px octicon + `<h2>` + `<p>`), styled already in the CSS.

### 1. `templates/repo/release/list.tmpl`
Add an `{{else}}` branch to the `{{range $idx, $info := .Releases}}` loop — but render the
placeholder **outside** the `<ul>` (a `<div>` inside `<ul>` is invalid HTML). Shape:

```
{{if .Releases}}
	<ul id="release-list"> …existing range unchanged… </ul>
{{else}}
	<div class="empty-placeholder">
		{{svg "octicon-tag" 48}}
		<h2>{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.release.empty"}}</h2>
		<p>{{if .CanCreateRelease}}{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.release.empty_description_writer"}}{{else}}{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.release.empty_description"}}{{end}}</p>
		{{if .CanCreateRelease}}
			<a class="ui small primary button" href="{{$.RepoLink}}/releases/new">{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.release.new_release"}}</a>
		{{end}}
	</div>
{{end}}
```
- Keep `{{template "base/paginate" .}}` where it is.
- `SingleRelease` also uses this template but always has one release, so it never hits the branch.
- Drafts are visible to writers via `.Releases`, so a repo with only drafts correctly shows the list.
- Minor edge (acceptable, note in PR): `?page=99` past the end also shows the empty state.

### 2. `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` (next to `repo.release.*`, ~line 2616)
- `repo.release.empty`: "No releases yet."
- `repo.release.empty_description`: "Releases package software versions for download. This repository has not published one yet."
- `repo.release.empty_description_writer`: "Create a release from a tag to publish a version of this repository."
Only en-US is edited (other locales come from Crowdin). Wording is a draft — Carson should reword.

### 3. Integration test in `tests/integration/release_test.go`
Rendering needs the full template stack, so an integration test (existing pattern:
`TestViewReleaseListNoLogin`). Fixture: `user5/repo4` (repo id 4, public, non-empty, no rows in
`models/fixtures/release.yml`). Subtests:
- `NoLogin`: GET `/user5/repo4/releases` → `.empty-placeholder` exists, `#release-list` absent,
  no `/releases/new` link.
- `Owner` (`loginUser(t, "user5")`): `.empty-placeholder a[href="/user5/repo4/releases/new"]` exists.
- Regression is already covered by `TestViewReleaseListLogin` (repo1 still lists 3 entries).

## Workflow
- Branch: `feat/issue-1-empty-releases-message` off `main`.
- Commit: `feat(repo): show empty state on releases page` with `Assisted-by: Claude Code:claude-opus-5` only (no Co-Authored-By / Signed-off-by).
- Afterward: capture the SpecStory log and post the per-issue "AI Assistance" comment.

## Verification (run in WSL via `wsync`)
- `wsync go test -tags 'sqlite sqlite_unlock_notify' -run '^TestViewReleases' ./tests/integration/` (or `make test-sqlite#TestViewReleaseList…`) — new test plus existing release list tests pass.
- `wsync make lint-templates` if available (check `make help`), and confirm no trailing whitespace.
- Manual: run Gitea, create an empty repo → Releases tab shows the message + "New Release" button;
  view as a logged-out user → message without the button; create a release → list returns.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-09-14 22:58:41Z)**_

Mostly right, with two corrections: one about wording, and one about what the second condition checks.

**1. "Added these release tags to the locale json"**: close, but they're **translation keys**, not tags. "Tags" means git tags on this page, so it's worth keeping the words apart. `locale_en-US.json` maps each key to its English text:
```json
"repo.release.empty": "No releases yet.",
```

**2. "Putting the release quote in the html"**: not quite. The template never contains the English text. It only names the key, and Gitea swaps in the text for the viewer's language when the page is built:
```
<h2>{{ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.release.empty"}}</h2>
```
That's why every visible string goes through a key: translators can supply other languages without touching the template.

**3. "Conditions to show which release note is shown based on if there are any releases"**: half right. There are two separate conditions, and they check different things:

| Condition | Checks | Decides |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{{if .Releases}}` | Are there any releases to show on this page? | The normal release list, or the empty message |
| `{{if .CanCreateRelease}}` | Can this viewer create releases? | Which description line is shown, and whether the **New Release** button appears |

So the choice of description depends on **the viewer's permission**, not on the release count. The count only decides whether the empty message shows at all.

Both values come from the `Releases()` handler in `routers/web/repo/release.go`, which puts them into `ctx.Data`:
- `ctx.Data["Releases"]` is set at line 191.
- `ctx.Data["CanCreateRelease"]` is set at line 173. It's true when the viewer can write to releases and the repo isn't archived.

The template can only use what the handler puts in `ctx.Data`, which is why no Go change was needed.

**4. Also part of the change**: the `TestViewReleaseListEmpty` integration test covers both permission cases. A logged-out visitor gets the message without the button, and the repo owner gets the button.

The earlier question still stands: should I commit so I can run the tests in WSL?

## Rerunning the tests yourself
From Git Bash in the Gitea folder. Remember `wsync` only sees committed changes:
```bash
# your new test only, verbose
wsync make 'test-integration#^TestViewReleaseListEmpty' GOTEST_FLAGS='-v -count=1'

# everything touching the releases template
wsync go test -count=1 -v -run '^(TestViewRelease.*|TestCreateRelease.*|TestViewSingleRelease|TestViewTagsList)$' gitea.dev/tests/integration
```
`-count=1` stops Go from reusing a cached result. Don't put a `|` inside a `make 'test-integration#…'` target: it breaks the command, so use `go test` directly for patterns like that.

## Reproducing the tests by hand on http://localhost:3001
The server is still running your branch. Each step matches a check in the test.

**Setup (the test data gives you this automatically: `user5/repo4`, which has commits but no releases):**

2. Open `carso/test` and add a README or new file through the web UI. The repo needs at least one commit, or Releases returns a 404 (the `MustBeNotEmpty` guard).
3. Don't create any releases or tags yet.

**Owner view, matches the `Owner` subtest:**
4. Go to http://localhost:3001/carso/test/releases.
5. You should see a tag icon, **"No releases yet."**, the line "Create a release from a tag to publish a version of this repository.", and a **New Release** button.
6. Right-click → Inspect: the button sits inside `<div class="empty-placeholder">` and links to `/carso/test/releases/new`. This is what the test's selector `.empty-placeholder a[href=".../releases/new"]` finds.

**Regression, covered by the existing tests:**

12. Optional: delete the release and its tag, and the message returns.

**Optional extra:** to see a test catch a real bug, temporarily change `{{if .CanCreateRelease}}` around the button to `{{if true}}`. Commit it locally and rerun the test: `NoLogin` should fail. Then undo it with `git reset --hard HEAD~1`, which throws away that throwaway commit.

```text
# Student Guide — Running Gitea Locally

Welcome! This is a course fork of [Gitea](https://about.gitea.com/), a self-hosted Git service
written in **Go** (backend) and **Vue/TypeScript** (frontend). You'll be improving the kind of tool
you use every day — issues, pull requests, code review, CI/Actions.

This guide gets you from a fresh clone to a running Gitea on your machine, backed by **SQLite** (no
separate database server needed). It should take ~15–30 minutes, most of which is the first backend
compile.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

Install these before you start. Versions below are the minimums this fork is pinned to.

| Tool | Version | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Go** | **1.26.4+** | Backend. `go.mod` requires `go 1.26.4`. |
| **Node.js** | **22.18.0+** | Frontend build only (not needed at runtime). |
| **pnpm** | **11.0.0+** | Frontend package manager. Easiest via `corepack enable`. |
| **Git** | 2.x | Required both to build **and at runtime** (Gitea shells out to git). |

> 💡 **New to Go?** Gitea's backend is written in Go. [A Tour of Go](https://go.dev/tour/) is the official interactive tutorial (~2 hours) and covers everything you need for typical backend tasks. Pay attention to goroutines and interfaces — both appear frequently in this codebase.
> 📖 **Developer docs:** [`docs/development.md`](docs/development.md) in this repo covers the development workflow, how to run tests, database migration conventions, and the overall package structure. Read it before picking a task.

**You do NOT need a C compiler (gcc).** This version of Gitea uses a pure-Go SQLite driver
(`modernc.org/sqlite`) and builds with `CGO_ENABLED=0`, so there's no MSYS2/MinGW/Xcode-tools step.
This is the main reason setup is painless on Windows.

**Optional:** `make` (convenience only — every command below also has a no-`make` form), and Docker
(if you'd rather run the official container instead of building).

### Installing the toolchain

- **Windows:** `winget install GoLang.Go` and `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS`, then `corepack enable`.
- **macOS:** `brew install go node` then `corepack enable`.
- **Linux:** use your package manager (or the official Go tarball) for Go + Node, then `corepack enable`.

Verify:

```bash
go version      # go1.26.x
node --version  # v22.18+ (or newer)
pnpm --version  # 11.x
git --version
```

---

## 2. Get the code

```bash
git clone https://github.com/musta55/gitea.git
cd gitea
```

---

## 3. Build

Gitea is built in two halves: the frontend assets (with pnpm/vite) and the backend binary (with Go).

### Option A — with `make` (recommended if you have it)

```bash
make build          # builds frontend + backend into ./gitea (or gitea.exe on Windows)
```

### Option B — without `make` (works everywhere)

```bash
# 1) frontend assets -> public/assets/
pnpm install
pnpm exec vite build

# 2) backend binary  (pure-Go SQLite, no gcc)
#    Linux/macOS:
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o gitea .
#    Windows (PowerShell):
$env:CGO_ENABLED=0; go build -buildmode=exe -o gitea.exe .
```

> The first backend compile takes a few minutes and produces a ~100+ MB binary. Later builds are fast.

---

## 4. Run (SQLite, zero config)

Just start the web server from the repo root and let the built-in installer set everything up:

```bash
# Linux/macOS:
./gitea web
# Windows:
./gitea.exe web
```

Then open **http://localhost:3000** and you'll see the **Install** page:

1. **Database Type:** choose **SQLite3** (the default path is fine).
2. Leave the rest at defaults for local dev.
3. Expand **Administrator Account Settings** and create your admin username / password / email
   (do this now so you don't have to register separately).
4. Click **Install Gitea**.

That's it — you now have a running Gitea with a SQLite database at `data/gitea.db`. Log in with the
admin account you just created.

> **Port already in use?** If something else owns `:3000`, start Gitea on another port:
> `./gitea web --port 3030` and open http://localhost:3030 instead.

### On macOS

The same `./gitea web` command works — a few Mac-specific notes:

- **Firewall prompt:** the first launch may ask *"Do you want the application `gitea` to accept
  incoming network connections?"* — click **Allow** (it's the binary you just built).
- **`permission denied`:** make the binary executable first: `chmod +x gitea`.
- **Gatekeeper "cannot be opened" warning:** only affects binaries downloaded from a browser, not
  ones you built yourself. If you ever run a downloaded release binary instead, clear the
  quarantine flag: `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ./gitea`.
- **Apple Silicon (M1–M4):** fully supported — Go produces a native arm64 binary, nothing extra to do.

### Live-reload while developing (optional)

If you have `make`:

```bash
make watch          # rebuilds frontend + backend on file changes (uses air)
```

---

## 5. Try it out

Create a repository (with "Initialize repository"), open an issue, push a branch, and open a pull
request so you can see the code-review UI. These are the areas most course tasks touch:

- **Code review UI** — the diff viewer and PR review flow.
- **Issues / Kanban** — issue tracking and project boards.
- **CI / Actions** — the built-in Actions runner and workflow UI.

---

## 6. Running the tests

Gitea's test suite is validated on **Linux CI**. Run it on Linux, macOS, WSL2, or the provided
`.devcontainer` — **not native Windows**, where a handful of unit tests fail for platform reasons
(symlink semantics, temp-file cleanup) rather than real bugs.

```bash
# unit tests
CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./...
# or, with make:
make test-backend         # unit tests
make test-integration     # integration tests (defaults to SQLite via GITEA_TEST_DATABASE)
```

Frontend tests:

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run
```

---

## 7. Common gotchas

- **`git` not found at runtime:** Gitea runs git commands for every repo operation. Make sure `git`
  is on your `PATH`, not just in your IDE.
- **`go build` is slow the first time:** normal — it compiles ~3000 packages once, then caches.
- **Don't commit build artifacts:** `gitea`/`gitea.exe`, `data/`, `custom/`, and `public/assets/*`
  are gitignored. Keep them out of your commits.
- **Windows line endings:** the repo expects LF. Your editor/`.gitattributes` should keep it that way.

---

---

## Contributing workflow

All team members have write access to this repository, so the team uses a **branch-based** workflow — not forks. Here is the background and the commands.

**Why not forks?** Forking is the standard model for contributing to open-source projects where you *don't* have write access: you fork to your own GitHub account, clone your fork, and open a PR from your fork back to the original. You will encounter this when contributing to the upstream project. But for your course team — where everyone has write access to the shared repo — it just adds confusion: two clones on your machine, two remotes to keep in sync, merge conflicts that are harder to reason about.

**Branch-based workflow** is what most professional teams use internally. You clone the shared repo once, create a short-lived branch for each issue, push the branch back to the same repo, and open a PR from that branch into `main`. One clone, one remote, full PR workflow.

### For each issue you work on

```bash
# One-time setup: clone the team repo (skip if already done)
git clone https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea.git
cd gitea

# Before starting each issue: make sure you are on a fresh main
git checkout main
git pull origin main

# Create a branch named for the issue
git checkout -b feat/issue-17-dark-mode      # new feature
git checkout -b fix/issue-42-toast-dismiss   # bug fix

# ... make your changes, run tests ...

# Stage and commit
git add <the files you changed>
git commit -m "feat: add dark mode toggle (#17)"

# Push the branch to the team repo
git push origin feat/issue-17-dark-mode
```

After pushing, GitHub shows a **"Compare & pull request"** banner on the repository page. Click it to open a PR from your branch into `main`. Fill in the description (what changed and why), reference the issue (`Closes #17`), and request a review from a teammate.

**Branch naming:**

| Prefix | Use for |
| --- | --- |
| `feat/issue-<N>-short-description` | new features |
| `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` | bug fixes |
| `chore/short-description` | docs, config, dependency updates |

> ⚠️ **`main` is protected — direct pushes are blocked.** All changes go through a reviewed PR. If you accidentally commit to `main` locally, move your changes to a branch before pushing:
>
> ```bash
> git checkout -b fix/issue-42-my-fix   # create branch from your current state
> git checkout main
> git reset --hard origin/main          # revert local main to match remote
> ```

**After your PR is merged**, delete the branch to keep the repo tidy:

```bash
git checkout main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feat/issue-17-dark-mode
```

## 8. Project documentation & policies (required reading)

📚 **Official documentation:** <https://docs.gitea.com/> — usage, administration, and development
guides.

Gitea has its own established contribution processes. They are **not restated here** — you are
responsible for finding, reading, and following them from the sources below:

| You must take care of | Where to find it |
| --- | --- |
| How to use the tool | <https://docs.gitea.com/> |
| Code review process | [CONTRIBUTING.md — Code review](CONTRIBUTING.md#code-review) |
| Bug / issue resolution process | [CONTRIBUTING.md — How to report issues](CONTRIBUTING.md#how-to-report-issues) |
| Pull request conventions & PR policies | [CONTRIBUTING.md — Pull request format](CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request-format) + [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (commit/PR conventions) |
| AI policies | [CONTRIBUTING.md — AI Contribution Policy](CONTRIBUTING.md#ai-contribution-policy) + [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) |
=====README
# .claude-students — start here

Course-only documentation for the CSCI-435 Gitea fork. It exists so a person — or an AI session —
can read one or two short pages instead of exploring ~150 Go packages. That exploration is the
single largest avoidable cost on this project, in your time and in tokens.

This page is the quick start: what is here, what tools you have, and the three things you will
actually need to do.

## Two layers, same content

| | `docs/` | `guide/` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Written for | an AI session | a person |
| Style | terse, every claim cites a file | explains, defines jargon, names symptoms |
| Length | ~80 lines | up to 200 |
| Status | **the source of truth** | a rendering of it |

Both have the same 34 filenames, so `guide/models-db.md` explains `docs/models-db.md`.

**`guide/` is derived from `docs/`.** Each guide stores a fingerprint of its source page, so if the
reference changes and the guide is not regenerated, the validator says so. **If the two ever
disagree, the guide is wrong** — fix the reference page, not the guide.

## What is in this folder

| File | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| `INDEX.md` | Routing table: "working on X → read Y". Loaded into every AI session. |
| `guide/START-HERE.md` | **If you are new to this codebase, read this first.** |
| `guide/*.md` | A plain-English page per reference page. |
| `docs/*.md` | The reference pages. Terse, citation-heavy. |
| `MAINTENANCE.md` | The 22 rules. Read before editing anything here. |
| `_TEMPLATE.md`, `guide/_TEMPLATE.md` | The only permitted shapes for a new page. |
| `check.sh` | The validator. Run it before you push. |

## Your toolkit

One command:

```sh
./.claude-students/check.sh
```

It prints `check.sh: ok (34 docs, guide 34/34)` when everything is fine, or `file: message (rule N)`
for each problem. It is dependency-free and finishes in under a second.

It checks, among other things: that every page follows its template, stays under its line cap, cites
only paths that exist, and is listed in `INDEX.md`; that no two reference pages claim the same code;
that **every guide matches the fingerprint of its source page**; and that a guide cites no path its
source page does not — so a guide can add explanation, but never new facts.

## The three things you will actually do

### 1. You are new and want to understand the codebase

Read `guide/START-HERE.md`, then `guide/architecture.md`, then `guide/testing.md`. After that, read
only the page for whatever you are touching. Do not read all 34.

`INDEX.md` maps tasks to pages.

### 2. You found a page that is wrong or incomplete

This is expected, and fixing it is part of the work — not a favour.

1. Fix **`docs/<name>.md`**, never the guide. Every claim needs a repo path; no line numbers, only
   file plus symbol name.
2. Regenerate **`guide/<name>.md`** to match, and update its `source-hash` to the first 16
   characters of `sha256sum .claude-students/docs/<name>.md`.
3. Run `./.claude-students/check.sh`.
4. Ship both in the same pull request as the code change that taught you this, titled
   `docs(context): <subject>`.

If you skip step 2 the validator will tell you, by name, on the next run.

The easiest way to do step 2 is to ask an AI session: *"`docs/<name>.md` changed — regenerate
`guide/<name>.md` from it and update the hash."*

### 3. You are starting a fresh AI session

You do not have to do anything. `CLAUDE.md` imports `INDEX.md`, so every Claude session already has
the routing table, and `AGENTS.md` points other tools at it.

If a session starts exploring the tree instead of reading a page, say: *"Read
`.claude-students/INDEX.md` and use the page for this area."*

If you ask a session to change documentation here, point it at `MAINTENANCE.md` — rules 16-22 are
the ones about keeping the two layers in step.

## Not upstream

This folder is **ours**, not Gitea's, and is deliberately self-contained so it can be removed in one
step if this fork is ever merged upstream:

```sh
rm -rf .claude-students/
```

Then remove the two pointers: the `@.claude-students/INDEX.md` line in `CLAUDE.md`, and the
`.claude-students/INDEX.md` bullet in `AGENTS.md`. Nothing else refers to this folder — no
`Makefile` target, no CI job.

## Authority

These pages never override the project's own rules. `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and
`docs/guidelines-*.md` at the repository root are authoritative; the pages here summarise them and
point at code. If a page here contradicts one of those, the page here is wrong.

Note that `docs/` means two different things depending on where you are standing: inside this
folder it is our reference pages, at the repository root it is Gitea's own documentation. The guides
say "in this folder" or "Gitea's own" wherever it could be ambiguous.
=====MAINT
<!-- markdownlint-disable MD029 -->
<!-- Rules are numbered continuously 1-15 across the sections below; check.sh error
     messages and all 34 docs cite them by number, so the sequence must not restart. -->

# Maintenance rules

Five people maintain one shared set of docs. These rules exist so the set stays *one* set. Read
them before editing anything in `.claude-students/`. Rules marked **[checked]** are enforced by
`./.claude-students/check.sh`.

## Scope discipline

1. **Upstream wins.** `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/guidelines-*.md` are authoritative.
   Docs here summarise them and link to them; they never restate a rule differently and never
   contradict one. A contradiction is a bug in this folder, not in the project.
2. **One fact, one home.** Every fact lives in exactly one doc — the one whose `scope:` owns that
   path. Everywhere else, link to it. Duplicated facts are how five maintainers end up with five
   different answers.
3. **Durability test.** Record a fact only if it (a) took more than one discovery step to find and
   (b) will still be true after the next upstream merge. A one-off workaround, a sprint detail or
   anything about your own task fails this test — that belongs in `ai-logs/`.
4. **No process notes.** No TODOs, no open questions, no first person, no student names, no dates
   other than `verified-at`. This is a map of the code, not a journal.

## Form

5. **Template only [checked].** Use the `## ` headings from `_TEMPLATE.md`, all of them, in that
   order, with nothing added. If a section has nothing to say, write one line saying so.
6. **120-line cap [checked].** Going over means the scope is too broad. Split the doc, and add the
   new `INDEX.md` row in the same commit. `INDEX.md` itself is capped at 60 lines.
7. **Cite or delete [checked, partially].** Every claim names a repo path. A claim with no path is
   unverifiable by the next reader — delete it.
8. **Symbols, not line numbers [checked].** Write `models/db/context.go` → `WithTx`, never
   `models/db/context.go:143`. Line numbers rot at the next upstream merge and a stale number is
   worse than no number. Code fences stay at 10 lines or fewer — point at the file instead of
   copying it.
9. **Repo-relative paths [checked].** `models/db/context.go`, never `/home/you/gitea/models/...`.
10. **Whitespace [checked].** No trailing whitespace, LF endings, final newline — same as the rest
    of the repo (`.editorconfig`).

## Change control

11. **One universal set.** These docs live on `main` and nowhere else. Never keep a personal copy,
    a per-student folder, or a long-lived branch of them.
12. **Changes land by PR**, titled `docs(context): <subject>` per `AGENTS.md` Conventional Commits,
    with an `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer and no `Co-Authored-By` or
    `Signed-off-by`.
13. **Fix in place.** If you discover while working that a doc is wrong or incomplete, correct it
    in the *same* PR as your code change and update `verified-at` to the commit you checked
    against. Leaving a doc stale for someone else to hit is the exact failure this folder exists to
    prevent. This rule applies to AI sessions too.
14. **New docs need three things in one commit [checked]:** the file, its `INDEX.md` row, and a
    `scope:` that does not overlap any existing doc's. If the scope overlaps, you wanted to edit
    that doc, not add one.
15. **`./.claude-students/check.sh` passes before you push [checked].** It is dependency-free and
    finishes in under a second.

## The guide layer (rules 16-22)

`guide/` holds a plain-English page for each reference page in `docs/`, same filename. It exists so
a person new to Go and to this codebase can get oriented. It is **derived**, not independent.

16. Every guide carries `source:`, `source-hash:` and `verified-at:` in its frontmatter **[checked]**.
17. A guide's `source:` names a real `docs/*.md` with the **same filename** **[checked]**.
18. `source-hash:` is the first 16 characters of `sha256sum docs/<name>.md`. If the reference page
    changes and the guide is not regenerated, `check.sh` reports **drift** **[checked]**. Regenerating
    means: reread the reference page, rewrite the guide, update the hash and `verified-at`.
19. Guide headings match `guide/_TEMPLATE.md` exactly and in order **[checked]**.
20. Guides are capped at **200 lines**, code fences at **30** **[checked]** — teaching needs more room
    than reference does.
21. **A guide adds explanation, vocabulary and worked steps. It adds no new facts.** Every repo path
    a guide cites must also be cited by its source page **[checked]**. If you need a fact the
    reference page lacks, add it *there* first, which bumps the hash and forces the guide to be
    regenerated in the same commit — exactly the intended order.
22. `guide/START-HERE.md` has no source page. It is exempt from rules 17, 18 and 21, and is where
    cross-cutting material lives that no single reference page owns.

**Never fix a fact in `guide/`.** If the two layers disagree, the reference page is the truth and
the guide is stale: fix `docs/`, regenerate the guide, ship both in one PR. A disagreement is a bug
report against `docs/`, not an editing job in `guide/`.

**Known limitation:** a hand-edit to a guide that only rewords prose is not mechanically
detectable. Rule 21 catches invented facts; rule 18 catches a stale guide; review catches the rest.

## Updating `verified-at`

`verified-at` is the short SHA the doc was last checked against, from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.
Bump it whenever you confirm or correct a doc. A doc whose `verified-at` is far behind `main` has
not been checked recently — treat its details as hints and confirm them in the code before relying
on them.

146	## Code review
147	
148	How labels, milestones, and the merge queue work is documented in [docs/community-governance.md](docs/community-governance.md).
149	
150	### Pull request format
151	
152	Please try to make your pull request easy to review for us. \
153	For that, please read the [*Best Practices for Faster Reviews*](https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/261cb0fd089b64002c91e8eddceebf032462ccd6/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#best-practices-for-faster-reviews) guide. \
154	It has lots of useful tips for any project you may want to contribute to. \
155	Some of the key points:
156	
157	- Make small pull requests. \
158	  The smaller, the faster to review and the more likely it will be merged soon.
159	- Don't make changes unrelated to your PR. \
160	  Maybe there are typos on some comments, maybe refactoring would be welcome on a function... \
161	  but if that is not related to your PR, please make *another* PR for that.
162	- Split big pull requests into multiple small ones. \
163	  An incremental change will be faster to review than a huge PR.
164	- Allow edits by maintainers. This way, the maintainers will take care of merging the PR later on instead of you.
165	
166	### PR title and summary
167	
168	In the PR title, describe the problem you are fixing, not how you are fixing it. \
169	Use the first comment as a summary of your PR. \
170	In the PR summary, you can describe exactly how you are fixing this problem.
171	
172	PR titles must follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format, because PRs are squash-merged and the PR title becomes the resulting commit message:
173	
174	```text
175	type(scope)!: subject
176	```
177	
178	The scope in parentheses is optional. A `!` immediately before the colon marks a [breaking change](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/#summary): either `type!:` or `type(scope)!:` (not `type!(scope):`).
179	
180	Use one of these types:
181	
182	- `build`: Changes affecting the build system, packaging, or external dependencies
183	- `ci`: Changes to CI/CD configuration files and scripts
184	- `chore`: Maintenance changes that do not affect production code or should not appear in the changelog
185	- `docs`: Documentation-only changes
186	- `feat`: A larger user-facing feature, improvement, or new functionality
187	- `enhance`: Small or trivial user-facing improvements or UX polish (for example wording changes, color adjustments, spacing or padding tweaks, placeholders, small UI behavior improvements)
188	- `fix`: A bug fix, UX correction, or security-related dependency update
189	- `perf`: Performance improvements (speed, memory, scalability)
190	- `refactor`: A code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature
191	- `revert`: Reverts a previous change
192	- `style`: Formatting or style-only changes that do not affect code behavior (for example lint-driven edits)
193	- `test`: Adding or correcting tests
194	
195	Examples:
196	
197	```text
198	fix(web): prevent avatar upload crash on empty file
199	feat(api): add pagination to repo hooks list
200	enhance(repo): improve diff toolbar spacing
201	ci(workflows): lint PR titles in CI
202	```
203	
204	Keep this summary up-to-date as the PR evolves. \
205	If your PR changes the UI, you must add **after** screenshots in the PR summary. \
206	If you are not implementing a new feature, you should also post **before** screenshots for comparison.
207	
208	If you are implementing a new feature, your PR will only be merged if your screenshots are up to date.\
209	Furthermore, feature PRs will only be merged if their summary contains a clear usage description (understandable for users) and testing description (understandable for reviewers).
210	You should strive to combine both into a single description.
211	
212	Another requirement for merging PRs is that the PR is labeled correctly.\
213	However, this is not your job as a contributor, but the job of the person merging your PR.\
214	If you think that your PR was labeled incorrectly, or notice that it was merged without labels, please let us know.
215	
216	For pull requests that use a valid Conventional Commits title, CI automatically applies a matching `type/…` label when the title prefix is `feat`, `enhance`, `fix`, `docs`, or `test` (for example `enhance(web): …` receives `type/enhancement`).\
217	That label is kept in sync with the PR title when the title is edited.\
218	Other title prefixes do not get an automatic `type/…` label; the merger still assigns the correct labels (including `type/…` when needed) for changelog and backport decisions.
219

## Summary

When a repository has no releases, the Releases tab rendered only the header and an empty list, which looks like a broken page. This adds an empty state to that page.

### How it is fixed

- `templates/repo/release/list.tmpl`: the release list is wrapped in `{{if .Releases}}`. When there are no releases, an `empty-placeholder` block is rendered instead (the same pattern the Projects page uses): a tag icon, a "No releases yet." heading, and a description.
- The description depends on `.CanCreateRelease` (set by the `Releases` handler in `routers/web/repo/release.go`: write access to releases and repo not archived):
  - users who can create releases see a prompt to create one and a **New Release** button linking to `/releases/new`;
  - everyone else sees a short explanation of what releases are, with no button.
- `options/locale/locale_en-US.json`: three new keys, `repo.release.empty`, `repo.release.empty_description`, `repo.release.empty_description_writer`.
- No handler or model changes; the template already had all the data it needed.

### Usage

Open **Releases** on any repository that has commits but no releases. Maintainers see a message and a New Release button; visitors see a message only. Once a release exists, the normal list is shown.

### Screenshots

### Testing

New integration test `TestViewReleaseListEmpty` in `tests/integration/release_test.go`, using the `user5/repo4` fixture (has commits, no releases):

- `NoLogin`: the `.empty-placeholder` renders, `#release-list` is absent, and there is no `/releases/new` link.
- `Owner`: logged in as `user5`, the placeholder contains the New Release link.

Ran locally (WSL, SQLite), all passing:

```sh
go test -count=1 -v -run '^(TestViewRelease.*|TestCreateRelease.*|TestViewSingleRelease|TestViewTagsList)$' gitea.dev/tests/integration
```

Manual check on a local instance: repo with a commit and no releases shows the message and button as owner, message only in a private window, and the list returns after creating a release.

### Notes for reviewers

- A repository with **no commits** still returns 404 on `/releases` because of the existing `MustBeNotEmpty` guard in `routers/web/web.go`; this PR does not change that. The empty state covers repositories with commits but no releases.
- Requesting a page past the end (e.g. `?page=99`) also shows the empty state.
- Only the `{{if}}`/`{{else}}` lines were added around the existing `<ul>`; the list markup was not re-indented to keep the diff small.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-09-14 23:46:10Z)**_

No. Translation keys are a general technique called **internationalization (i18n)**, and almost every language and framework has a version of it. The idea is always the same: code refers to a stable **key**, and a separate file per language maps that key to the text people see.

| Ecosystem | Where the text lives | How code asks for it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Gitea (Go)** | `options/locale/locale_en-US.json` | `ctx.Locale.Tr "repo.release.empty"` |
| Java (your Software Dev background) | `messages_en.properties` | `ResourceBundle.getString("release.empty")` |
| JavaScript / React / Vue | `en.json` via i18next or vue-i18n | `t('release.empty')` |
| Python / Django, C, Linux apps | `.po` files (gettext) | `_("No releases yet.")` |
| Android | `res/values/strings.xml` | `R.string.release_empty` |
| iOS | `Localizable.strings` | `NSLocalizedString(...)` |

**Why use keys instead of writing the text directly:**
- **Translators never touch code.** They edit a file of strings per language. Gitea gets those from Crowdin, which is why you only edited `en-US`.
- **One place to change wording.** The key `repo.release.new_release` is used in three templates, and changing its text changes all three.
- **A fallback language.** A missing translation falls back to English instead of breaking the page.

**How it works in Gitea specifically:**
- **Loading:** at startup, `InitLocales` in `modules/translation/translation.go` reads every `locale_*.json` file. English is the base (`locale_en-US.json`); other languages fill in on top of it.
- **Picking a language:** each request uses the viewer's language, and `ctx.Locale.Tr` looks up the key in it.
- **Plurals:** `ctx.Locale.TrN` picks singular or plural. That's how the header shows "0 Releases" but "1 Tag".
- **The frontend uses the same keys.** Vue/TypeScript code doesn't read the JSON files. The Go template sends it strings that are already translated. For example, `templates/base/head_script.tmpl` builds `window.config.i18n` with `ctx.Locale.Tr "error.occurred"`. The comment there says page-specific text should reach the frontend through HTML `data-` attributes, `PageData`, or API responses rather than that global object.

So Go does the lookup here, but a project in almost any other language would use the same pattern.

This covers a case the automated test doesn't: signed in, but not allowed to create releases. Registration is enabled on your local server.

98		cred, err := wa.WebAuthn.FinishRegistration(webAuthnUser, *sessionData, ctx.Req)
99		if err != nil {
100			if pErr, ok := err.(*protocol.Error); ok {
101				log.Error("Unable to finish registration due to error: %v\nDevInfo: %s", pErr, pErr.DevInfo)
102			}
103			ctx.ServerError("CreateCredential", err)
104			return
105		}
106	
107		dbCred, err := auth.GetWebAuthnCredentialByName(ctx, ctx.Doer.ID, name)
108		if err != nil && !auth.IsErrWebAuthnCredentialNotExist(err) {
109			ctx.ServerError("GetWebAuthnCredentialsByUID", err)
110			return
111		}
112		if dbCred != nil {
113			ctx.HTTPError(http.StatusConflict, "Name already taken")
114			return
115		}
116	
117		// Create the credential
118		_, err = auth.CreateCredential(ctx, ctx.Doer.ID, name, cred)
119		if err != nil {
120			ctx.ServerError("CreateCredential", err)
121			return
122		}
123		_ = ctx.Session.Delete("webauthnName")
124		_ = ctx.Session.Set(session.KeyUserHasTwoFactorAuth, true)
125		ctx.JSON(http.StatusCreated, cred)
126	}
127	
128	// WebauthnDelete deletes an security key by id
129	func WebauthnDelete(ctx *context.Context) {
130		if user_model.IsFeatureDisabledWithLoginType(ctx.Doer, setting.UserFeatureManageMFA) {
131			ctx.HTTPError(http.StatusNotFound)
132			return
133		}
134	
135		if _, err := auth.DeleteCredential(ctx, ctx.FormInt64("id"), ctx.Doer.ID); err != nil {
136			ctx.ServerError("GetWebAuthnCredentialByID", err)
137			return
138		}
139		ctx.JSONRedirect(setting.AppSubURL + "/user/settings/security")
140	}
141

94	// to convert protocol.AuthenticatorFlags to webauthn.CredentialFlags
95	func newCredentialFlagsFromAuthenticatorFlags(flags protocol.AuthenticatorFlags) webauthn.CredentialFlags {
96		return webauthn.CredentialFlags{
97			UserPresent:    flags.HasUserPresent(),
98			UserVerified:   flags.HasUserVerified(),
99			BackupEligible: flags.HasBackupEligible(),

105	func (list WebAuthnCredentialList) ToCredentials(defaultAuthFlags ...protocol.AuthenticatorFlags) []webauthn.Credential {
106		// TODO: at the moment, Gitea doesn't store or check the flags
107		// so we need to use the default flags from the authenticator to make the login validation pass
108		// In the future, we should:
109		// 1. store the flags when registering the credential
110		// 2. provide the stored flags when converting the credentials (for login)
111		// 3. for old users, still use this fallback to the default flags
112		defAuthFlags := util.OptionalArg(defaultAuthFlags)
113		creds := make([]webauthn.Credential, 0, len(list))
114		for _, cred := range list {
115			creds = append(creds, webauthn.Credential{
116				ID:              cred.CredentialID,
117				PublicKey:       cred.PublicKey,
118				AttestationType: cred.AttestationType,
119				Flags:           newCredentialFlagsFromAuthenticatorFlags(defAuthFlags),
120				Authenticator: webauthn.Authenticator{
121					AAGUID:       cred.AAGUID,
122					SignCount:    cred.SignCount,
123					CloneWarning: cred.CloneWarning,
124				},
125			})
126		}
127		return creds

- **Setup:** it logs in as `user2` **first**, then creates two keys for user2 and one for user4. The order matters: if user2 had keys before logging in, login would stop and ask for the security key. The fixture file also says tests should create their own data rather than add fixtures.

| `NonexistentKey` | id 99999 | 404 | same response as above, so no info leaks |

## Before you start: two warnings
- **Registering a key turns on 2FA for your account.** The browser's fake authenticator (below) disappears when you close DevTools. If you sign out with a key still registered and DevTools closed, you can't sign back in. Either delete your keys before closing DevTools, or recover with:
  ```bash
  wsl -d Debian --exec bash -c 'cd ~/gitea && ./gitea admin user disable-2fa --username carso'
  ```
- **Use Chrome or Edge.** They have a built-in fake security key for testing, so you don't need a real YubiKey or Windows Hello.

## Setup: a fake security key in the browser
1. Open http://localhost:3001 and sign in as `carso`.
2. Press **F12**, then **⋮** (top-right of DevTools) → **More tools** → **WebAuthn**.
3. Tick **Enable virtual authenticator environment**, then **Add authenticator** with protocol `ctap2`, transport `internal`, and **Supports resident keys** and **Supports user verification** both ticked. Resident keys are required because Gitea registers passkeys.
4. Keep DevTools open for the whole session.

## Create test keys
5. Go to **Settings → Security** (http://localhost:3001/user/settings/security).
6. Under "Two-Factor Authentication (Security Keys)", type `Laptop Key` in **Nickname** and click **Add Security Key**. The fake authenticator answers automatically, and the key appears in the list with the new **Rename Security Key** button next to **Remove**.
7. Add a second key named `Phone Key`.

## Edge cases

**A. Normal rename** (`Success` test)
1. Click **Rename Security Key** on `Laptop Key`. The dialog opens with "Laptop Key" already filled in, from `data-modal-rename-webauthn-nickname`.
2. Change it to `Work Laptop` and click **Confirm**.
3. The page reloads with a green "The security key has been renamed." banner and the new name in the list.

**B. The key still works after renaming** ("without changing authentication behavior")
1. Sign out, with DevTools still open, and sign in again with your password.
2. Gitea asks for your security key and the fake authenticator answers, so login succeeds. This works because only the name changed, not the credential. In the WebAuthn panel the credential's sign count also goes up.

**C. Case change of its own name** (`CaseChangeOfOwnName`)
1. Rename `Work Laptop` to `WORK LAPTOP`. It saves, because the duplicate check ignores a match on the key being renamed.

**D. Name already used** (`NameTaken`)
1. Rename `WORK LAPTOP` to `phone key`, in lowercase.
2. The dialog stays open with a red "Another security key already uses this nickname.", and nothing changes. The check ignores case, just like the database's unique index.

**E. Blank name** (`InvalidNames`)
1. Clear the box and click **Confirm**. The **browser** blocks it first ("Please fill out this field") because of the `required` attribute.
2. To reach the **server** check, as a user bypassing the browser could: open the DevTools **Console** while the dialog is open and run
   ```js
   document.querySelector('#rename-webauthn-nickname').removeAttribute('required')
   ```
   Clear the box and **Confirm** again. The red error now comes from the server: "Nickname cannot be empty".

**F. Name too long** (`InvalidNames`)
1. With the dialog open, run in the Console:
   ```js
   const el = document.querySelector('#rename-webauthn-nickname'); el.removeAttribute('maxlength'); el.value = 'a'.repeat(256);
   ```
2. **Confirm**. The server rejects it with a length error that mentions Nickname. Try 255 characters (`'a'.repeat(255)`) and it saves, since that's exactly the column limit.

**G. Someone else's key** (`OtherUsersKey`)
1. In a **second browser profile or a different browser** (a private window shares no fake authenticator, which is fine here), register `testuser` at http://localhost:3001/user/sign_up. Add the same kind of fake authenticator in that window's DevTools and register a key called `Other User Key`.
2. Find its id: in DevTools **Elements**, click its Rename button and read `data-modal-form.url="/user/settings/security/webauthn/rename?id=N"`.
3. Back as `carso`, open the Rename dialog on one of your keys, then run in the Console (replace `N` with that id):
   ```js
   document.querySelector('#rename-webauthn-modal form').action = '/user/settings/security/webauthn/rename?id=N'
   ```
4. Type `Stolen` and **Confirm**. You get the red "The target couldn't be found." Reload `testuser`'s page and their key is still `Other User Key`.

**H. Key that doesn't exist** (`NonexistentKey`)
1. Repeat G.3 with `id=99999`. You get the same "couldn't be found" message, so an attacker can't tell a missing key from someone else's.

## Cleanup
- **Remove** your keys, and `testuser`'s, before closing DevTools, or use the `disable-2fa` command above.

**Screenshots for the PR:** capture the dialog with a name filled in (A), the name-taken error (D), and the list after renaming.

# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

3. Tick **Enable virtual authenticator environment**, then **Add** an authenticator with protocol `ctap2`, transport `internal`, and both **Supports resident keys** and **Supports user verification** ticked.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-09-15 01:01:08Z)**_

Yes, press **Add**. Then add the keys on the Gitea page, not in DevTools.

## In the DevTools WebAuthn panel
1. Tick **Enable virtual authenticator environment**.
2. Under **New authenticator**, set:
   - **Protocol:** `ctap2`
   - **Transport:** `internal`
   - **Supports resident keys:** ticked
   - **Supports user verification:** ticked
   - (leave the other options at their defaults)
3. Click **Add**. A section like "Authenticator 1" appears with an empty **Credentials** table. That's your fake security key.
4. **Leave DevTools open** from here on.

## On the Gitea page (left side of the window)
5. On http://localhost:3001/user/settings/security, scroll to the **Two-Factor Authentication (Security Keys)** section.
6. Under the list, there's a **Nickname** text box and an **Add Security Key** button.
7. Type `Laptop Key` in **Nickname** and click **Add Security Key**. There's no popup: the fake authenticator answers automatically, and the page reloads with **Laptop Key** in the list.
8. Type `Phone Key` in **Nickname** and click **Add Security Key** again.

## How to tell it worked
- **In Gitea:** both keys are listed, each with **Rename Security Key** and **Remove** buttons.
- **In DevTools:** the authenticator's **Credentials** table now has 2 rows.

If you see a red "unknown error" instead, the resident keys option probably wasn't ticked. Remove the authenticator, add it again with both options ticked, and retry.

Once both keys show up, continue with **edge case A** from the earlier steps.

Good news first: **edge case B passed.** The server log shows your sign-in succeeded with the renamed key:

```
21:03:44  POST /user/settings/security/webauthn/rename?id=1   200 OK   ← renamed key 1
21:04:12  POST /user/login                                   303      ← password accepted, 2FA required
21:04:12  GET  /user/webauthn/assertion                      200 OK   ← browser asked for the key
21:04:17  POST /user/webauthn/assertion                      200 OK   ← key accepted, you're signed in
21:05:13  POST /user/settings/security/webauthn/delete?id=2  200 OK   ← you removed key 2
21:05:20  POST .../webauthn/request_register                 200 OK   ← a new key registration started, not finished
```

The 200 on `/user/webauthn/assertion` means the renamed key worked for sign-in. That proves renaming didn't change the credential, which is the issue's "without changing authentication behavior".

## Why the popups looked different
- **Seeing a popup at all means the fake DevTools key didn't handle that request.** When the virtual authenticator environment is active, Chrome answers silently. So when you registered, Chrome used the real options on your PC instead, and picking **This device** most likely saved the key to Windows Hello or your Chrome profile.
- **Signing in is a different request with different options.** At registration Chrome offers every place it *could* create a key. At sign-in it only offers places where it expects your existing key to be, so the options can differ. I can't tell from the server log exactly why only USB was offered; it depends on Chrome, Windows, and whether the WebAuthn panel was active in that tab. Either way, the server accepted the key, so it worked for this test.

## Where you are now
- `carso` has 2FA **on**, with at least key 1 (the renamed one). A registration started at 21:05:20 never finished, so no key was saved from it.
- To avoid a confusing mix of Windows Hello and fake keys, either stick with what you have, or remove all keys and re-add them while the WebAuthn panel is open and enabled **in that same tab**. The sign that it's working: **no popup** when you click Add Security Key.

**Before you finish:** remove your keys in Settings → Security, including any saved to Windows Hello. If a sign-in ever gets stuck at the key prompt, run:
```bash
wsl -d Debian --exec bash -c 'cd ~/gitea && ./gitea admin user disable-2fa --username carso'
```

That's expected. It's the browser half of the length check working.

## What you're seeing
The dialog's text box has `maxlength="255"` (added in step 6). Once you reach 255 characters, Chrome ignores further key presses, and if you paste longer text it cuts it to 255. So by typing you can only reach 255 characters, which is valid, and saving it should work.

That's the convenience check. The **real** protection is the server's `MaxSize(255)` in `WebauthnRenameForm` (step 2). To see it, you have to get past the browser limit the way an attacker could, which is why step F uses the Console.

## Testing the server check
1. Open the **Rename Security Key** dialog on a key and leave it open.
2. In DevTools, click the **Console** tab. It's next to Elements at the top; if the WebAuthn panel covers it, look in the top tab row or the **»** menu.
3. Paste this and press **Enter**:
   ```js
   const el = document.querySelector('#rename-webauthn-nickname'); el.removeAttribute('maxlength'); el.value = 'a'.repeat(256);
   ```
   - If Chrome warns about pasting, type `allow pasting`, press Enter, and paste again.
   - The first line removes the browser's limit. The second fills the box with exactly 256 characters, one over.
4. Click **Confirm** in the dialog.

**Expected:** the dialog stays open with a **red error from the server** about the Nickname length, and the key's name doesn't change. That's the `InvalidNames` test case.

**Opposite boundary (optional):** run the same line with `'a'.repeat(255)` and confirm. It saves, because 255 fits the column exactly.

**If you'd rather not use the Console:** in the **Elements** tab, press **Ctrl + F** and search for `rename-webauthn-nickname`. Double-click `maxlength="255"` on the `<input>` line, delete it, and press Enter. You can then paste as much text as you like, for example 300 characters from a text editor.

**H checks that renaming a key that doesn't exist fails safely.** You change where the Rename dialog sends its request to a made-up key id, `99999`. Unlike G, you don't need a second account.

## Steps
1. Go to http://localhost:3001/user/settings/security, signed in as `carso` with DevTools open.
2. Click **Rename Security Key** on any of your keys, and leave the dialog open.
3. In DevTools, click the **Console** tab.
4. Paste this and press **Enter**. If Chrome asks, type `allow pasting` first.
   ```js
   document.querySelector('#rename-webauthn-modal form').action = '/user/settings/security/webauthn/rename?id=99999'
   ```
   The dialog's form now submits to key `99999` instead of the key you clicked. The Console echoes the URL back, which confirms the change took.
5. In the dialog, type `Missing` as the name and click **Confirm**.

## Expected result
- The dialog stays open and shows a **red "The target couldn't be found."**
- Close the dialog and reload the page: **none of your keys changed names**, and the real key you clicked still has its old name.

## Why this matters
- In `WebauthnRename`, `GetWebAuthnCredentialByID` finds no key with id 99999, so the handler returns `ctx.JSONErrorNotFound()` before it reaches the save step.
- This is the **same message** G gives for someone else's key. An attacker trying ids can't tell "doesn't exist" from "exists but isn't yours", so they can't discover which key ids belong to other people.
- It matches the `NonexistentKey` subtest in `TestUserSettingsWebAuthnRename`, which expects a 404 for id 99999.

**Optional check:** in DevTools **Network**, click the `rename?id=99999` request. The status is **404** and the response is `{"errorMessage":"The target couldn't be found.","renderFormat":"text"}`.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-09-15 01:15:01Z)**_

There's no bug in the rename code. **The id 99999 request never ran, because the browser wasn't signed in at that moment.** "Missing" was then saved to your real key on a later, normal rename.

## What the log shows
```
21:13:10  POST .../rename?id=99999  → answered by the login check (web.go:172)
21:13:10  GET  /user/login                ← sent to the login page
21:13:19  POST /user/login                ← you signed in again
21:13:26  POST /user/webauthn/assertion   ← security key accepted
21:13:31  GET  /user/settings/security    ← back on Settings → Security
21:13:35  POST .../rename?id=1  → WebauthnRename   ← normal rename of your real key
```

1. **At 21:13:10 you weren't signed in.** Your session had ended, probably from signing out and back in during B in another tab. The login check that guards all `/user/settings` pages (`verifyAuthWithOptions`, the `options.SignInRequired` branch) redirected the id 99999 request to the login page. `WebauthnRename` never ran, so nothing was saved from that request.
2. **You signed back in and returned to Security.**
3. **You clicked Rename again, which reset the dialog.** Each click on **Rename Security Key** fills the form's destination from that button (`data-modal-form.url="...?id=1"`), overwriting the Console change. So the `Missing` you submitted went to your real key, id 1, and a normal rename succeeded as it should.

## Retry H (order matters)
1. Reload http://localhost:3001/user/settings/security and make sure you're signed in (your avatar is top right).
2. Click **Rename Security Key** on a key, and leave the dialog open.
3. **Only now**, run this in the Console:
   ```js
   document.querySelector('#rename-webauthn-modal form').action = '/user/settings/security/webauthn/rename?id=99999'
   ```
4. **Without closing or reopening the dialog,** type `Missing2` and click **Confirm**.

**Expected:** a red **"The target couldn't be found."**, and no key named `Missing2`.

To confirm it reached your code this time, send me the new log line, or open DevTools **Network** → the `rename?id=99999` request. It should show status **404** and, in the server log, `@ security/webauthn.go ... WebauthnRename` instead of `verifyAuthWithOptions`.

The automated `NonexistentKey` test already checks this exact case and passed, so a 404 is what I expect to see.

## The big picture

```
Browser                                      Server
───────                                      ──────
[Rename Security Key] button  (template)
   │ opens dialog, fills name + key id
   ▼

                                                                        │ checks: feature on? form valid? your key? name free?
                                                                        ▼
                                                                     Model      (models/auth/webauthn.go)
                                                                        │ UPDATE name, lower_name WHERE id AND user_id
   ◄──────────── JSON: redirect (success) or errorMessage (failure) ───┘
Page reloads with green banner, or red error stays in the dialog
```

These are Gitea's layers: **template → route → form → handler → model → database**. Each file does one job, and every new piece copies the existing **register** or **delete** code for security keys.

## 1. Template: `templates/user/settings/security/webauthn.tmpl`

**The button**, added to each key in the list:
```html
<button class="ui tiny button show-modal"
    data-modal="#rename-webauthn-modal"
    data-modal-form.url="{{$.Link}}/webauthn/rename?id={{.ID}}"
    data-modal-rename-webauthn-nickname="{{.Name}}">
```
- **`show-modal`** is a class Gitea's shared JavaScript already handles (`web_src/js/features/common-button.ts`), so this feature needs **no new JavaScript**.
- **`data-modal`** says which dialog to open.
- **`data-modal-form.url`** sets where the dialog's form submits, including **this key's id**. That's why one dialog works for every key. It's also why, in edge case H, reopening the dialog reset your Console change.
- **`data-modal-rename-webauthn-nickname`** fills the text box with the current name.
- **`{{.ID}}` and `{{.Name}}`** come from the `WebAuthnCredentials` list the existing Security page handler already provides.

**The dialog**, one shared copy on the page:
```html
<form class="ui form form-fetch-action" method="post">
    <input id="rename-webauthn-nickname" name="name" type="text" maxlength="255" required>
```
- **`form-fetch-action`** is another existing pattern. It submits in the background, then either shows the server's error message or follows its redirect.
- **`name="name"`** must match the form struct's `Name` field (section 3).
- **`required` and `maxlength`** are only browser conveniences, as you saw in F. The server checks the same things again.
- **Text keys used:** the label reuses `settings.webauthn_nickname`, the title uses the new `settings.webauthn_rename_key`, and the button row is the standard `base/modal_actions_confirm` partial.

## 2. Route: `routers/web/web.go`
```go
m.Post("/rename", web.Bind(forms.WebauthnRenameForm{}), security.WebauthnRename)
```
- **One line, in the same `/webauthn` group as register and delete,** so the full URL is `/user/settings/security/webauthn/rename`.
- **Protection comes from the group.** It's inside `/user/settings`, which requires sign-in; that's the `verifyAuthWithOptions` check that redirected your signed-out request in H. It's a POST, so it also gets cross-origin protection (the `crossOriginProtection.Check` in that same function).
- **`web.Bind(...)` runs first:** it copies the posted `name` into the form struct and validates it, then the handler runs.

## 3. Form: `services/forms/user_form.go`
```go
type WebauthnRenameForm struct {
    Name string `binding:"Required;MaxSize(255)" locale:"settings.webauthn_nickname"`
}
```
- **`Required`** rejects a blank name (edge case E).
- **`MaxSize(255)`** rejects anything longer than the database column. A plain Go `string` becomes `VARCHAR(255)`; I checked this in the xorm source (edge case F).
- **`locale:`** makes error messages say "Nickname" instead of "Name".
- **`Validate()`** is copied boilerplate that connects the struct to Gitea's shared validation.

## 4. Handler: `routers/web/user/setting/security/webauthn.go` → `WebauthnRename`
It runs checks in order and stops at the first failure:

| Step | Code | On failure | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `IsFeatureDisabledWithLoginType(... ManageMFA)` | 404 | An admin can turn off 2FA management; copied from register/delete |
| 2 | `ctx.HasError()` | 400 + "Nickname cannot be empty" etc. | Reads what `web.Bind` found in step 3 |
| 3 | `GetWebAuthnCredentialByID` + `cred.UserID != ctx.Doer.ID` | 404 "The target couldn't be found." | **Ownership check.** A missing key and someone else's key get the same answer, so nothing leaks (G, H) |
| 4 | `GetWebAuthnCredentialByName` + `sameName.ID != cred.ID` | 400 "Another security key already uses this nickname." | Blocks duplicates, ignoring case (D), but allows changing only the capitalization of its own name (C) |
| 5 | `UpdateCredentialName(...)` | 500 | Saves the new name |
| 6 | `Flash.Success` + `JSONRedirect` | none | Green banner and reload, the same way delete ends |

`ctx.Doer` is the signed-in user. It's always set here because the route group requires sign-in.

## 5. Model: `models/auth/webauthn.go` → `UpdateCredentialName`
```go
db.GetEngine(ctx).ID(id).Where("user_id = ?", userID).Cols("name", "lower_name").Update(&WebAuthnCredential{Name: name})
```
- **`.ID(id).Where("user_id = ?", userID)`** only matches your own key. It's a second ownership check in case this function is ever called from somewhere without step 3's check.
- **`.Cols("name", "lower_name")`** changes **only** those two columns. The credential ID, public key and sign count stay the same, which is why signing in still worked in B.
- **`lower_name` is set automatically** by the existing `BeforeUpdate()` hook. A unique index on (`lower_name`, `user_id`) is the database-level reason step 4 exists.
- **Why it returns only `error`, unlike `DeleteCredential`'s `(bool, error)`:** on MySQL, saving an unchanged name counts as "0 rows changed", so a "changed or not" result can't reliably mean "not your key". That's why ownership is checked in the handler instead.

## 6. Text keys: `options/locale/locale_en-US.json`
| Key | Text |
| --- | --- |
| `settings.webauthn_rename_key` | Rename Security Key |
| `settings.webauthn_rename_key_success` | The security key has been renamed. |
| `settings.webauthn_nickname_taken` | Another security key already uses this nickname. |

They're added only to en-US; other languages come from Crowdin. "Nickname" was reused, not added.

## 7. Tests
**Unit test: `models/auth/webauthn_test.go` → `TestUpdateCredentialName`**
- Tests the model function alone, using the fixture key (id 1, owned by user 32).
- **User 2 renames it:** the name is unchanged, which proves the `user_id` filter.
- **User 32 renames it:** the name changes and `lower_name` is `"renamed key"`, which proves the hook ran.

**Integration test: `tests/integration/user_settings_test.go` → `TestUserSettingsWebAuthnRename`**
- Sends real HTTP requests through the whole path: route → form → handler → model.
- **It logs in before creating keys,** because otherwise login would require a security key.
- Every failure case also re-reads the database to prove nothing was saved:

| Subtest | Edge case | Expects |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Success` | A | 200 + redirect; name changed; credential ID unchanged |
| `CaseChangeOfOwnName` | C | Allowed |
| `InvalidNames` | E, F | 400 for blank and 256 characters |
| `NameTaken` | D | 400 + exact "already uses" message |
| `OtherUsersKey` | G | 404, other user's key unchanged |
| `NonexistentKey` | H | 404 |

## Choices a reviewer may ask about
1. **Why a dialog and not editing the name in place?** It reuses the existing `show-modal` and `form-fetch-action` patterns (see the Actions variables edit dialog), so it adds no JavaScript. That's the smallest change.
2. **Why 404 for another user's key instead of 403?** 403 would confirm the key exists. With 404, a missing key and someone else's look the same.
3. **Why check ownership in both the handler and the model?** The handler check gives the right error message. The model filter protects any future caller that forgets the check.
4. **Why is the model function different from `DeleteCredential`?** Because of the MySQL "0 rows changed" behavior above.
5. **Why doesn't registration get the 255 limit too?** It's out of scope for this issue. You could mention it as a possible follow-up.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-09-15 01:23:06Z)**_

I fixed it: a name made only of spaces is now rejected, and spaces around a real name are trimmed off before saving. The rename test passes, including a new subtest, and your local server is running the fix (version `98e73f51f3`).

## Why spaces got through
`Required` in the form library only checks whether the value is **exactly** empty. `"   "` isn't, so it passed. Your browser's `required` attribute has the same gap.

## The fix (in `WebauthnRename`)
```go
form.Name = strings.TrimSpace(form.Name)
if form.Name == "" { // "Required" binding only rejects an exactly empty value, not whitespace
    ctx.JSONError(ctx.Locale.TrString("settings.webauthn_nickname") + ctx.Locale.TrString("form.require_error"))
    return
}
```
- **`strings.TrimSpace`** removes spaces, tabs and newlines from both ends.
- **If nothing is left,** it returns the **same** "Nickname cannot be empty." that a blank name gets. It builds the message exactly the way the form library does (`trName + "form.require_error"`), so no new text key was needed.
- **Trimming happens before the duplicate check and the save.** `"  Laptop Key "` is saved as `Laptop Key`, and you also can't create a near-duplicate that differs only by a trailing space.
- **It uses `TrString` rather than `Tr`** so the message is sent as plain text, not HTML.

## Test changes (`TestUserSettingsWebAuthnRename`)
| Subtest | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `InvalidNames` | now also sends `"   "` and expects 400 with the name unchanged |
| `SurroundingSpacesTrimmed` (new) | `"  Spaced Key  "` is saved as `Spaced Key` |

All 7 subtests pass.

## Try it live
**Server check (bypassing the browser):**
1. Reload http://localhost:3001/user/settings/security and click **Rename Security Key**.
2. Type only spaces and click **Confirm**.
3. Expected: a red **"Nickname cannot be empty."**, and the name doesn't change.

**Trimming:**
1. Rename a key to `   Test Key   `.
2. It saves as `Test Key`. Open the Rename dialog again to confirm there are no leading spaces.

## Git
I added this as a **second commit** rather than changing the first, as AGENTS.md asks:
```
98e73f51f3 fix(user): reject whitespace-only security key nicknames
aff9a20450 feat(user): allow renaming security keys
```
Neither commit is pushed yet.

**For your PR:**
- **Testing section:** add this edge case.
- **Notes for reviewers:** say that `Required` doesn't reject whitespace, which is why the handler trims.

**One mistake on my side:** my first rebuild ran `make` in WSL without `wsync`, so it failed and the server briefly restarted on the old build. I rebuilt through `wsync` and confirmed the version.
